R. s. 10</cite>; <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 5:8">Koh. R. to V, 8</cite> <cite ref="C00129"><he>גבר</he></cite>, corr. acc.) a charmer (of snakes) came; Tanḥ. Ḥuck. 1.—Pl. <he>חַבָּרַיָּא</he>.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 65b:17">Snh. 65ᵇ</cite> <he>מן ח׳ את</he> thou art a creation of the charmers.
<cite ref="Gittin 16b">Gitt. 16ᵇ</cite>, sq. <he>אתא ההוא ח׳ וכ׳</he> a Parsee came and took the lamp from them.—Pl. <he>חַבָּרֵי</he>.
<cite ref="Shabbat 45a:2">Sabb. 45ᵃ</cite> <he>מקמי ח׳</he> from fear of the Parsees (that they might see the lights).
<cite ref="Yevamot 63b:9">Yeb. 63ᵇ</cite> <he>אתו ח׳ לבבל</he> the Parsees have entered the Jewish colonies of Babylonia.
<cite ref="Beitzah 6a:5">Bets. 6ᵃ</cite> but nowadays <he>דאיכא ח׳</he> when there are Parsees (forcing to public labors).
